user_direction.ingredient_scope: Bok choy ingredient only; exclude added cooking oil; do not label as complete dish nutrition.

candidate_sources.publisher: Japan Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
candidate_sources.database: Standard Tables of Food Composition in Japan, 2023 Supplement
candidate_sources.record: 06160; Vegetables / Green bok choy / leaves, raw
candidate_sources.official_reuse_observation: MEXT says food-composition data may be freely used and requests that secondary use in articles, books and applications identify the source as the 2023 supplement.
candidate_sources.food_scope_observation: The official record explicitly says leaves, raw; it is not a verified whole-plant bok choy record.
candidate_sources.decision: Rights conditions appear clear for the data under the stated citation instruction, but the record scope does not match the whole visible ingredient. Do not use it as a whole-bok-choy or cooked-portion profile.

observations: The official page says the last update was 2021-03-19 and that some older foods remain in a separate file without review or validation in later updates.
The GOV.UK footer states that content is under Open Government Licence v3.0 except where otherwise stated.
candidate_sources.food_record_status: No exact raw whole-bok-choy record was verified from the official workbook in this batch; third-party search results were not accepted as authoritative proof of the row.
candidate_sources.decision: Keep as a possible source pending official-row and third-party-rights verification; not admitted and not used for nutrition.

api_food_record_test.request_scope: Food-description endpoint only; nutrientamount endpoint was not called and no nutrient values were retrieved.

api_capabilities: Official guide documents JSON/XML API access for reuse in applications.
Nutrient amount endpoint describes mean nutrient values per 100 g edible portion and returns nutrient source ID, standard error and number of observations.
Health Canada's current overview says the online searchable CNF 2015 remains available while a more user-friendly way to access the CNF 2026 dataset is being developed.
candidate_sources.cnf_2015_reuse_observation: The official 2015 user guide says commercial and non-commercial use is allowed without further permission, requests Health Canada attribution, says nutrient values must not be modified but may be expressed in different serving sizes, and requires as-is, non-endorsement and reference-only context.
candidate_sources.cnf_2026_reuse_observation: Open Government Portal metadata for the 2026 dataset reports Open Government Licence - Canada and links its licence. This batch did not retrieve or inspect the dataset files, verify the 2026 row 2038, or clear any record-level third-party material.
candidate_sources.decision: Strongest current alternative candidate, but not admitted. Keep the 2015 API and 2026 downloadable dataset as separate reuse routes; verify version-specific record, lineage and delivery/retention obligations before use. A direct authoritative API could be more deterministic than Tavily extraction for this known record, but no architecture change is approved.

cross_cutting_constraints: A raw 100 g food record does not become an exact nutrient profile for the image-estimated cooked grams of a stir-fried portion.
If only ingredient reference values are available, label the source preparation and per-100-g basis; do not present them as a complete dish or exact cooked serving.
The raw CNF record may overlap with USDA-derived data; inspect nutrient source IDs and local USDA matching before treating it as independent evidence or a new fallback layer.
Using a specific direct government API may reduce search and model parsing uncertainty, but changing the planned TFDA -> USDA -> Tavily/model flow requires an explicit architecture decision.

decision.reason: CNF presents a promising, more explicit reuse path and an exact raw food-name match in the legacy API, but the latest 2026 record lineage, exact source-version licensing details, USDA overlap, local routing eligibility, and photo-portion conversion are not yet verified.

next_gate: Verify whether CNF 2026 contains code 2038 with the same food description and inspect its nutrient source IDs without inferring missing values as zero.
Compare code 2038's provenance against the project's USDA/FDC source so a duplicated USDA-derived profile is not misrepresented as independent evidence.
Decide whether a source-specific official API belongs inside the third-layer source registry or whether general Tavily/model web extraction remains the intended fallback.

Only after rights, source identity, field semantics and portion scope are documented may an isolated nutrient-response test be run; keep production registry and automatic fallback disabled until admission review.
review_limits: This is a technical source and licence-document review, not legal advice.
CNF food code 2038 was verified against the current online API response, which Health Canada identifies as the 2015 CNF online; the same row was not verified in the 2026 downloadable dataset.
The CNF 2026 Open Government Licence metadata does not by itself clear third-party source components or prove that the legacy API and current dataset have identical rights conditions.
No nutrient values were requested from CNF, MEXT or CoFID in this batch.
